summary: The repo exists and I cloned it with full history (75 MB, 169 commits, HEAD 8ba59f0), to /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-lukegogogo-claude-code-projects---2----/db472532-d13c-48f5-a638-abe179791f90/scratchpad/repos/harshilmathur__openra2. It is a legally clean, well-engineered, AI-built (Claude-orchestrated) TypeScript engine under GPL-3.0-or-later that can read RA2/YR data files. Everything I ran passes: install, tsc build, typecheck, lint, Vite production build, and 1954 portable tests. But as a game it is a small vertical slice. You can play 1v1 Soviet-vs-Soviet skirmish with 7 buildings (NACNST, NAPOWR, NAREFN, NAWEAP, NAHAND, NARADR, NALASR) and 4 units (SMCV, HARV, HTNK, E2), on 2 retail maps (Dustbowl, Arena) in 2 theaters (temperate, urban). There are no Allies, no Yuri faction, no aircraft, no naval units, no superweapons, no garrisons, no bridges, no campaigns or triggers, no multiplayer, no save/load, no FMV and no map editor. One architecture caveat matters a lot for a web remaster. All asset decoding (MIX to SHP/TMP atlases, VXL voxels pre-rendered into 32-facing sprites, rules to JSON, audio) runs in Node, inside a Vite dev-server middleware. So the `vite build` output is not a working standalone web page. The renderer is plain Three.js r169 WebGL with unlit MeshBasicMaterial quads: no custom shaders, lights or post-processing. That makes it easy to understand and extend, but none of the 2026-style visual stack exists yet. It already has a working AI-art HD sprite pipeline (gpt-image-1 buildings drawn at native footprint through `renderScale`). That pipeline is a useful prototype of the look you want, but it only runs in 'Original' mode, and the art is new designs, not remasters of the retail sprites. As a base for a faithful full-RA2 HD remaster, it would still need most of the game to be written.

tech_stack:
TypeScript 5.x strict monorepo using npm workspaces (package-lock v3). Node >= 20.19; CI tests Node 20.19 and 22, and I ran it on Node 26.0.0 / npm 11.12.1. Build is `tsc -b` for the packages plus Vite 7.3.6 for the client, with Vitest 3.2 and ESLint 9 + typescript-eslint 8. Runtime dependencies: only three@0.169.0 (@types/three 0.169). There is NO React, despite the discovery note and ROADMAP M6 saying "sidebar UI (React)". The HUD, sidebar, menu and minimap are hand-written DOM/TS (apps/client/src/hud.ts, sidebar.ts, menu.ts, minimapView.ts). Audio is WebAudio; sim timing uses an inline Web Worker heartbeat. Dev-only generator scripts call the OpenAI Images API (gpt-image-1) and TTS (gpt-4o-mini-tts). Size is about 46k lines of non-test TS/MJS (131 non-test .ts files, about 2.1 MB including dev .mjs scripts) plus 137 test files.

Packages:
- @vanguard/formats: file decoders.
- @vanguard/sim: deterministic core.
- @vanguard/game: rules projection and the bot.
- @vanguard/render: Three.js.
- @vanguard/client: Vite app plus the Node asset middleware.
renderer_architecture:
VERIFIED in code.

1) Where decoding happens. It runs in Node, not the browser. apps/client/vite.config.ts registers assetPlugin() (apps/client/dev/assetPlugin.ts). Its `configureServer` mounts `/assets/*` middleware (assetPlugin.ts:151-160). There is no `configurePreviewServer`, and the client fetches everything from `/assets/...` (apps/client/src/net.ts:85, assets.ts:61-263, menu.ts:420, hud.ts:871).
   - AssetSource (apps/client/dev/assetSource.ts) reads RA2_DIR/ra2.mix + ra2md.mix and mounts nested mixes into a Vfs (conquer, cache, local, isotemp, tem, isourb, urb, urban, sidec01/02, generic, cameo + conqmd, cachemd, localmd, isotemmd, isourbmd, genermd, cameomd).
   - MIX decoding: packages/formats/src/mix (CRC ids, Blowfish + Westwood RSA headers, ported from XCC).
   - SHP(TS): shp/shpDecode.ts + shpFile.ts. The server's dev/sprite.ts converts it into an RGBA color atlas plus a parallel grayscale remap-mask atlas and serves it in a binary format (JSON header line + raw RGBA).
   - TMP: tmp/tmpFile.ts. dev/terrain.ts + theater.ts build one per-map theater tile atlas with slope/height metadata.
   - PAL: pal/palFile.ts, 6-to-8-bit expansion as in XCC; palettes are applied server-side.
   - VXL + HVA: vxl/vxlFile.ts, hvaFile.ts, vxlNormals.ts. dev/voxelRender.ts is a CPU software rasterizer: HVA × section transform, rotation per facing, RA2 dimetric projection, z-buffer, Lambert lighting (ambient + diffuse from a fixed top-left light using the VXL normal tables), 2× supersampling. It produces 32-facing body atlases plus separate turret/barrel atlases (voxelCache.ts), so vehicles on screen are pre-rendered sprites, not meshes.
   - CSF: csf/csfFile.ts, used for display names.
   - INI: ini/iniFile.ts (FinalAlert2 tokeniser port). rules/rulesDb.ts builds typed rules, and game/src/toSimRules.ts projects a hand-listed slice into SimGameRules.
   - MAP (.map/.mpr/.yrm/.mmx/.yro): map/mapFile.ts, isoMapPack.ts (LZO), overlayPack.ts (LCW).
   - AUD/IDX/BAG: aud/*, played through WebAudio (apps/client/src/sound.ts, soundBridge.ts).
   - Video: none (no .bik/.vqa code).

2) Renderer: packages/render/src/scene/renderer.ts:413 `new THREE.WebGLRenderer({ canvas, antialias:false, alpha:true, preserveDrawingBuffer:true })` on three r169, which means WebGL2 (INFERENCE from three's release history: WebGL1 support was dropped in r163). There is no WebGPU.
   - Camera: one OrthographicCamera looking down -Z at a 1:1 pixel plane with pan and zoom. The iso math is in packages/render/src/iso/transform.ts (60×30 diamond; sx=(cx-cy)*30, sy=(cx+cy)*15 - z*15). Depth uses the painter's algorithm through renderOrder plus a Z value from depthKey.
   - Terrain: packages/render/src/scene/terrain.ts is one merged BufferGeometry of textured diamond quads in one draw call; ore is a second merged mesh of tinted diamonds, a placeholder for the real ore art.
   - Entities: scene/entities.ts (1,594 lines) uses pooled per-entity textured quads with their own MeshBasicMaterial each (no instancing), plus shadows, HP bars and pips.
   - Effects: scene/effects.ts uses pooled SHP-frame quads for muzzle flash, piff, explomed and explolrg, plus tracers.
   - Shroud: scene/fog.ts is a bordered DataTexture with LinearFilter feathering.
   - Every material is MeshBasicMaterial: no ShaderMaterial, no lights, no EffectComposer or post-processing, no tone mapping.
   - Textures are DataTextures with NearestFilter (scene/textures.ts:51-52, 101-102).
   - Team color is a CPU pre-tint: bakeTintedRgba (textures.ts) lerps house dark→light by the mask value and caches one texture per (atlas, house).
   - DPR-aware sizing uses setPixelRatio(devicePixelRatio).
   - No sub-tick interpolation (loop.ts:6, entities.ts:27): units draw at tick positions.
   - The sim runs on the main thread at 15/30/45 tps, default 45 (3×).
   - HD overlay path: SpriteAtlas.renderScale (render/src/assets/types.ts; used in entities.ts:523-530, 1068-1105) lets a high-res PNG draw at the retail iso footprint.

3) Sim and netcode: packages/sim is bitwise-deterministic. It uses Q16.16 fixed-point math, a PCG32 SimRng, and an FNV-1a SyncHash over all state, with a reflection-completeness test. The step function is `advance(world, orders)` in world/advance.ts:410. Replays are seed plus order stream (sim/src/replay/replay.ts) with golden-master tests. There is NO network layer: net.ts only fetches assets.

feature_completeness:
Checklist (V = verified in code, R = README/ROADMAP claim only):

- Soviet campaign: NO (V).
- Yuri's Revenge content: NO faction or units (V). It reads YR data (rulesmd.ini, artmd.ini, aimd.ini via ra2md.mix, which is required). ROADMAP: "Yuri explicitly deferred".
- Skirmish vs AI: YES, limited (V).
  - 1v1 on a Soviet-only roster, spawning at waypoints 0 and 1.
  - Bot (packages/game/src/bot): baseBuilder with a fixed BUILD_ORDER, harvesters per refinery, squadManager attack waves using aimd TaskForces weighted by TeamType Priority, a defender, and a no-op scout.
  - Easy, normal and hard differ only in data parameters.
  - AI quality: basic scripted waves (INFERENCE).

- Naval units & water: NO naval (V). World water cells are "passable to naval only". Original mode has procedural water tiles, but there is no water shader.
- Bridges: NO (V).
- Garrisoning: NO (V). "garrison" appears only in bot comments.
- Veterancy: YES (V), in sim/game/combat.ts and rules.ts: rookie/veteran/elite, ROF/armor/firepower/speed multipliers.
- Chronosphere / Iron Curtain / special abilities: NO (V).
- Fog & shroud: YES (V), in sim/game/fog.ts and render/scene/fog.ts. Retail shroud-only by default, full fog opt-in.
- Custom maps (.map/.mpr/.yrm): parser YES (V, formats/src/map/mapFile.ts handles .map/.mpr/.yrm/.mmx/.yro). In practice NO: the retail menu is whitelisted to MENU_MAPS = ['Dustbowl','Arena'] (apps/client/src/menuParams.ts:11), only temperate and urban theater mixes are mounted, and terrain passability is approximate ("densifyPassability").
- Sound / EVA / music: YES (V), with AUD/IDX/BAG decoding plus WebAudio (formats/src/aud, apps/client/src/sound.ts, soundBridge.ts, dev/audioSource.ts).

- Performance at high resolution: DPR-aware (V). Draws are per-entity MeshBasicMaterial quads with no instancing and no render interpolation. Headless self-play is fast (6000 ticks in 1.4 s). I did not browser-benchmark it at 3456×2234.
- Also present (V): MCV deploy, placement rules, power, sidebar queues with 4 tabs, ore economy with harvester docking, A* pathing plus collision, turret slewing, damaged building states, buildup animations, minimap with radar gating, control groups, win/lose overlay, game-speed setting, and an 'Original' zero-asset mode.
asset_requirements:
Classic mode (VERIFIED in apps/client/dev/assetSource.ts):
- It needs a legally owned RA2 **and** YR install. Both RA2_DIR/ra2.mix and RA2_DIR/ra2md.mix are read at top level and are required.
- Nested mixes used: conquer, cache, local, isotemp, tem, isourb, urb, urban, sidec01, sidec02, generic, cameo from ra2.mix; conqmd, cachemd, localmd, isotemmd, isourbmd, genermd, cameomd from ra2md.mix.
- Audio: audio.mix/language.mix, audiomd.mix inside langmd.mix, and theme.mix/thememd.mix (dev/audioSource.ts).
- Maps are loose .mmx/.map/.yrm files in RA2_DIR.

How you supply them: set RA2_DIR on the Node dev server (`RA2_DIR=/path/to/ra2 npm run dev --workspace @vanguard/client`) or put it in an untracked apps/client/.env.local. There is no in-browser upload, File System Access API or IndexedDB cache. Files are read server-side and never copied into the repo.

Original mode needs no game files. It serves committed art: 26 MB under apps/client/public/hd plus 6.8 MB of chrome, all AI or procedurally generated.

INFERENCE: for a real web product you would port the Node pipeline to a browser Web Worker fed by user-selected MIX files. The formats package is already pure TS; only png.ts and hdBuildings.ts use node:zlib and node:fs.
hd_extensibility:
Concrete plug-in points (V = verified hook exists, I = inference/estimate):

1) Hi-res sprite replacement. EASY–MEDIUM.
- (V) The hook already exists. SpriteAtlas.renderScale (packages/render/src/assets/types.ts; consumed in packages/render/src/scene/entities.ts:523-530, 1068-1105, 1277) draws a high-res PNG at the retail iso footprint.
- (V) The server side is loadHdBuilding (apps/client/dev/hdBuildings.ts) and the `/assets/sprite/hd/<TYPE>` route (sendHdSprite in assetPlugin.ts). The client tries HD first (apps/client/src/assets.ts:61-75).
- (V) The generator apps/client/dev/genHdBuildings.mjs (gpt-image-1) already does prompt → PNG → alpha-trim → manifest.
- (V) Blocker 1: HD art is locked to Original mode ("ALWAYS 404 for a classic (retail) request", locked by apps/client/dev/classicPure.test.ts). You would add a third "Remastered" mode that layers HD art over retail rules and maps.
- (V) Blocker 2: HD art is single-frame. It has no buildup, active-anim, damaged or 32-facing frames, and no team-color mask, while tinting depends on a remap mask (textures.ts bakeTintedRgba). Every HD sprite needs a matching mask plane.
- (I) Switch textures from NearestFilter to Linear + mipmaps + SRGBColorSpace (textures.ts:51-52, 101-102).

2) Voxel upgrade (VXL → real-time mesh). MEDIUM–HARD.
- (V) Today apps/client/dev/voxelRender.ts and voxelCache.ts rasterize in software, on the Node server, into 32-facing atlases at 2× supersampling.
- (I) Option A, cheap: raise the supersampling factor and facing count, and also emit normal and depth atlases, since the rasterizer already computes a z-buffer and per-voxel normals.
- (I) Option B, real: a client-side greedy or cube mesher from VxlFile sections using vxlNormals.ts, with HVA animation as bone transforms, drawn as THREE.Mesh in the ortho scene. That means reworking entities.ts's quad-only draw path and the painter's-order depth (renderOrder/depthKey), and replacing CPU pre-tint with shader tinting.

3) Normal/depth-map lighting. MEDIUM–HARD.
- (V) No lights exist and every material is MeshBasicMaterial (entities.ts:754-796, terrain.ts:236-257, effects.ts:343-357, props.ts:83).
- (I) Needs a custom ShaderMaterial or three TSL NodeMaterial for sprites, sampling color + normal + depth + team mask, and a light buffer for dynamic point lights (muzzle flashes, Tesla, fires) and time-of-day. Normals come from AI-generated normal maps or the voxel pre-render. Map [Lighting] sections are not parsed yet.

4) Post-processing. EASY–MEDIUM.
- (V) A single WebGLRenderer is created in packages/render/src/scene/renderer.ts:413 and render() is one pass.
- (I) Wrap it in EffectComposer (three/examples/jsm/postprocessing) or pmndrs/postprocessing: bloom, ACES tone mapping, color grading LUT, vignette, SMAA. Depth-based effects need a proper depth or G-buffer pass. Also upgrade three r169 → current for WebGPURenderer and TSL; the API surface used is small (I).

5) Water shader. MEDIUM.
- (V) Terrain is one merged mesh with atlas UVs (packages/render/src/scene/terrain.ts buildTerrain). Water cells are known from the sim grid (world.ts, "passable to naval only").
- (I) Split water cells into a second mesh with an animated normal-map, Fresnel, shoreline-foam and depth-tint shader. Naval gameplay does not exist, so this is visual only.

6) Weather. MEDIUM.
- (I) Add a new screen-space layer in renderer.ts (rain/snow GPU particles, fog, wet-ground tint, lightning flashes), plus global color grading. Nothing exists today.

7) GPU particles and impacts. MEDIUM.
- (V) packages/render/src/scene/effects.ts EffectSystem/EffectsLayer pools SHP-frame quads, with 4 effect slots (flash, impactSmall, impactLarge, explosionBig).
- (I) Replace or augment it with an instanced GPU particle system (InstancedBufferGeometry or three.quarks) for smoke, sparks, debris, shockwaves and scorch decals. The sim emits ShotFired and death events, which are already bridged in apps/client/src/effects.ts.

8) Prerequisite for any web release. MEDIUM.
- (I) Move the /assets conversion (apps/client/dev/assetPlugin.ts, about 63 KB) into a browser Web Worker with user-supplied MIX files and an IndexedDB cache.

Overall: the architecture is clean for the renderer (it reads sim state and never writes it; guardrail hash in loop.ts). But the modern visual stack would be built almost from scratch on top of it.
risks: It covers only a small fraction of RA2/YR. It has 11 of 100+ unit/building types and no Allies, Yuri, aircraft, naval, superweapons, garrisons, bridges, campaigns, triggers, multiplayer, save/load or FMV. Step 1 ('original functionality first') would mostly be new engine work, not porting.
The asset pipeline runs only in the Node Vite dev server (`configureServer` middleware). The production `vite build` output cannot load any assets, so it is not a deployable web game yet.

It was maintained by one author, fully AI-agent-generated (every commit co-authored by 'Claude Fable 5'), with no commits since 2026-07-27 and a single unanswered issue. Its bus factor is 1, and it could be abandoned.

Large monolithic files (entities.ts 1,594 lines; hud.ts 72 KB; controls.ts 74 KB; combat.ts 74 KB; economy.ts 71 KB) with very dense comments. Adding factions means working through systems written around the slice.

The strict determinism contract (no floats, SyncHash completeness test, golden-master regeneration protocol) raises the cost of every sim change, although it is what later makes lockstep multiplayer possible.
The renderer has no shaders, lights, post-processing, instancing or interpolation. Vehicles are pre-rendered sprites, not meshes, so the 2026-level visual target means building a new rendering layer.

The existing HD/AI-art mode is deliberately isolated from retail assets (classic-pure lock), and its art is new designs, not faithful HD versions of the retail sprites. An HD look true to the original needs a new pipeline.

Legal: the project is GPL-3.0-or-later, so derivatives must stay GPL. A 'faithful HD' remaster made by feeding retail EA sprites into image models would be derivative of EA copyright: fine for personal use, risky to distribute. EA trademark exposure also comes from the 'openra2' name and the RA2 branding.
Classic mode requires both RA2 and Yuri's Revenge files (ra2.mix and ra2md.mix). Only the temperate and urban theaters are mounted, and the menu hard-whitelists the Dustbowl and Arena maps.
Discovery claims were partly wrong: the client does not use React (it is plain DOM), and 'runs in the browser' holds only for the sim and renderer, not asset decoding.
score_rationale:
Scores by criterion:
- Legality/licensing: excellent, about 10/10. It is original, GPL-3.0-or-later with correct upstream attribution (XCC GPL-3.0, EA FinalAlert2 GPL-3.0, minilzo-js GPL-2.0-or-later), with a clean-room policy and no Chrono Divide lineage.
- Code quality/testability: strong, about 8/10. Everything builds, typechecks and lints cleanly; 1954 tests pass; there is CI and a deterministic sim with replays; renderer and sim are cleanly separated.
- Completeness of original gameplay: very weak, about 1.5/10. It is a Soviet-only 1v1 skirmish slice with 11 types on 2 maps; everything the user remembers beyond that (Allies, Yuri, naval, air, superweapons, campaigns, multiplayer) is missing.
- Renderer upgradability: moderate, about 5/10. The Three.js layer is simple and readable, with a working renderScale HD-sprite hook and an AI-art generator pipeline. But it has no shaders, lighting or post-processing, voxels are pre-rendered on the server, and assets depend on a Node dev server.
- Activity/community: weak, about 2/10. One author, 12 stars, dormant for 2 months.

For THIS project (a faithful full RA2 first, then an HD remaster, built on an existing web version rather than from scratch), it offers a legally safe foundation and a proof of concept for the AI-art look. It does not offer the 'existing working RA2' the user has in mind: most of step 1 would still be greenfield engine work. It is a reasonable choice only if legal cleanliness outranks everything and we accept building most of the game ourselves (possibly with AI agents, as its author did). Weighted, that gives 4/10.
